_meta.purpose: Maps a BOTS export's known attack timeline/storyline to the SAT-SA benchmark scenarios it should be paired with in workflow_augmentation, once a real BOTS export is available to fill this in.
_meta.status: TEMPLATE -- not filled in against a real dataset
_meta.why_not_filled_in: This development environment has no practical way to download an actual Splunk BOTS dataset export (registration-gated, multi-gigabyte, distributed as a Splunk index snapshot, not a simple file). Filling in real event counts, timelines, or storyline-specific detail here without ever having seen the actual data would itself be a fabrication -- exactly what public_benchmarks/__init__.py's honesty boundary forbids. This file instead documents the SCHEMA a real mapping should have, so a user with local BOTS access can populate it directly against the actual dataset rather than needing to design the format themselves.
_meta.how_to_fill_in: For each BOTS dataset version you have local access to: run public_benchmarks.bots.ingest_adapter.convert_jsonl against your exported notable events, inspect the resulting alert categories/severities/timeline, and record one 'bots_source' entry below naming which real storyline segment (by your own inspection of the actual data) you are pairing with which workflow_augmentation scenario_id.

supported_source_datasets.name: Splunk BOTS v1
supported_source_datasets.public_reference: https://github.com/splunk/botsv1 (dataset access via Splunk's BOTS program, not this repository)
supported_source_datasets.notes: Publicly known to be the smallest/oldest of the three BOTS releases; exact event counts and storyline detail intentionally not asserted here -- see _meta.why_not_filled_in.

supported_source_datasets.name: Splunk BOTS v3
supported_source_datasets.notes: Publicly documented to include cloud (AWS) infrastructure telemetry alongside traditional host/network sources; exact event counts and storyline detail intentionally not asserted here -- see _meta.why_not_filled_in.

mapping_entry_schema.bots_storyline_segment: string -- your own description of which real events you selected, e.g. 'notable events tagged search_name=Suspicious AWS Login Activity, timeframe <start>-<end>'
mapping_entry_schema.paired_scenario_id: string -- must match a scenario_id in workflow_augmentation/policy.yaml
mapping_entry_schema.filled_in_by: string -- who verified this against the real dataset
